autumn-bough.heading: Autumn Sweet Bough. Late Bough. Sweet Bellflower. Fall Bough. Philadelphia Sweet. White Sugar ?
autumn-bough.flavour: Flesh white, very tender, with a sweet, refreshing, vinous flavor.
autumn-bough.quality: One of the very best dessert sweet Apples of its season.
autumn-bough.storage: Last of August to first of October.
autumn-bough.note: Listed under Autumn Sweet Bough, with our synonyms Late Bough, Fall Bough, Sweet Bellflower, Philadelphia Sweet.

clarke-pearmain.heading: Clarke Pearmain. Yellow Pearmain. Columbian Russet. Gloucester Pearmain. Golden Pearmain.
clarke-pearmain.flavour: Flesh yellow, rather firm, crisp, rich, subacid.
clarke-pearmain.note: 'From North Carolina, an old variety.' Subacid rather than sweet, but not a clear contradiction of our 'sweet'.

coccagee.heading: Coccagee. Cocko Gee.
coccagee.note: 'An Irish Apple, mostly valued for cider.' Short entry after Hogg.

styre.heading: Forest Styre. Styre. Stire.
styre.note: 'A cider fruit, from Gloucestershire, England.' Short entry after Lindley (who in fact gives no taste).

poveshon.heading: Poveshon.
poveshon.note: 'An old New Jersey Apple, valued mainly for making early cider.' Small, oblate, deep red.

red-autumn-calville.heading: Red Autumn Calville. Calville Rouge d'Automne. Calville Rouge. Calville d'Automne. Pomme Violette. Erd Beere, or Strawberry of Switzerland.
red-autumn-calville.flavour: Flesh white, tender, juicy, often stained with red, sprightly aromatic, subacid.
red-autumn-calville.note: Synonyms include 'Pomme Violette' and 'Erd Beere, or Strawberry of Switzerland' (Rosseau, incorrectly). Downing calls it 'An unprofitable variety.'

swazie.heading: Swazie Pomme Grise. Pomme Grise d'Or.
swazie.flavour: flesh tender, juicy, mild subacid, rich and aromatic
swazie.note: Appendix entry, badly OCR'd. Probably originated on the Colonel Swazie farm near Niagara; 'more oblong, more golden in color, and more aromatic than the Pomme Grise, and is considered superior to it.'
